title: OCR overlay route has no local authentication or caller authorization check
reasoning: The SDK OCR overlay endpoint accepts a network request containing user-controlled image/query data, runs OCR, and returns an overlay artifact without any visible route-level authenticated user, session, permission dependency, or authorization decision in the included route implementation. If this SDK router is exposed without an enclosing global auth guard, callers can invoke OCR/overlay rendering directly. Because only this file is available, global middleware could exist elsewhere, so confidence is medium rather than high.
recommendation: Require the same authenticated SDK/session dependency used for protected SDK endpoints, or document and test that the router is always mounted behind a global auth dependency. Pass caller identity into the route if image sources or artifact access need per-user authorization.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for this feature, and the shown implementation has no assertion-visible auth dependency at the route boundary.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FastAPI route test for POST /api/sdk/ocr/overlay that verifies unauthenticated requests are rejected, or, if auth is enforced globally, a router-mount test proving the SDK router includes the required global dependency.
minimumFixScope: Route dependency or router mount/auth configuration plus focused API tests for unauthenticated and authenticated overlay requests.
